title: 细胞如何获取能量：代谢的两半
topic: How cells obtain and use energy through metabolism

sentences.en: Today let's look at how a living cell keeps running, because every organism, from a bacterium to a whale, faces one question: where does energy come from?
sentences.zh: 今天我们来看看一个活细胞是怎么维持运转的，因为每一种生物体，从细菌到鲸鱼，都面对同一个问题：能量从哪里来？

sentences.en: The sum of all the chemical reactions inside a cell is what we call metabolism, which has two halves.
sentences.zh: 一个细胞内部所有化学反应的总和，就是我们所说的新陈代谢，而它有两半。

sentences.en: One half breaks large molecules down to release energy; the other uses it to build new material.
sentences.zh: 一半把大分子分解以释放能量；另一半用这些能量去构建新物质。

sentences.en: None of it is fast enough to keep you alive without enzymes, proteins that act as biological catalysts.
sentences.zh: 如果没有酶——充当生物催化剂的蛋白质——这一切都不会快到足以让你活着。

sentences.en: An enzyme speeds a reaction thousands of times, yet is not used up, so it works again and again.
sentences.zh: 酶能把反应加快数千倍，自身却不被消耗，所以它可以一次又一次地工作。

sentences.en: When you eat, enzymes help you digest food, cutting starch and protein into molecules your gut can absorb.
sentences.zh: 你进食时，酶帮你消化食物，把淀粉和蛋白质切成你肠道能吸收的小分子。

sentences.en: Those nutrients cross the cell membrane and are broken down by respiration, which is why we respire, taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide.
sentences.zh: 这些养分穿过细胞膜，被呼吸作用分解，这正是我们呼吸的原因——吸入氧气、呼出二氧化碳。

sentences.en: The instructions for building every enzyme sit in the nucleus, in the cell's DNA, which directs protein-making.
sentences.zh: 构建每一种酶的指令都存在细胞核里，存在细胞的 DNA 中，由它来指挥蛋白质的合成。

sentences.en: Green plants add photosynthesis: a leaf captures sunlight and turns carbon dioxide and water into sugar, an organic molecule, plus oxygen.
sentences.zh: 绿色植物还多出光合作用：叶片捕获阳光，把二氧化碳和水转化成糖——一种有机分子，并释放出氧气。

sentences.en: This energy is controlled partly by hormones, chemical messengers that a gland secretes into the blood.
sentences.zh: 这份能量的调控有一部分靠激素——激素是腺体分泌到血液中的化学信使。

sentences.en: Not every cell runs at full speed: a seed can lie dormant for years, and even an embryo grows in bursts as its tissue forms each organ.
sentences.zh: 并非每个细胞都全速运转：一粒种子可以休眠数年，就连胚胎也是一阵一阵地生长，其组织一个器官接一个器官地成形。

sentences.en: When an organism dies, bacteria and fungi decompose the body, breaking that tissue into simple nutrients that return to the soil.
sentences.zh: 当一个生物体死去，细菌和真菌会分解遗体，把那些组织拆成简单的养分，回到土壤。

sentences.en: Any specimen under a microscope shows these pathways are ancient and shared, a clue that all species evolved from one ancestor and adapted the same chemistry.
sentences.zh: 在显微镜下，任何一份标本都显示这些通路古老而共通，这是一条线索，表明所有物种都从同一个祖先演化而来，只是把这套化学机制加以适应。

sentences.en: A virus is the odd exception: it has no metabolism and must hijack a host cell to reproduce, so your immune system treats it as an intruder.
sentences.zh: 病毒是个奇怪的例外：它没有代谢，必须劫持宿主细胞才能繁殖，所以你的免疫系统把它当作入侵者。

sentences.en: So keep this in mind: a cell that can capture energy, respire, build proteins, and reproduce is what being alive means.
sentences.zh: 所以请记住：一个能够捕获能量、进行呼吸、构建蛋白质并繁殖的细胞，就是「活着」的含义。
